public_rationale: OpenAI's release evaluation reports higher hallucination rates for o3 than o1 on both PersonQA and SimpleQA. This supports the comparison and the observation that hallucinations persisted. The report also finds more correct answers from o3; the claim should not be extended to mean that o3 was less accurate on every measure or that future progress was impossible.
limitations: These are provider-reported results on two factual-question benchmarks.
The report does not establish a universal hallucination rate across tasks or a rate per individual assertion.
The event date identifies the evaluated release; individual test execution dates are not supplied.

our_interpretation: Read 'not going away' as persistence at the time of the post, rather than a separate prediction that hallucinations can never be reduced.
Read 'more' as a higher measured hallucination rate on comparable factual-question evaluations against at least one earlier OpenAI model.
Use the April 2025 release reporting period through the post date for the ongoing observation about 'recent o3'.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations available for the release show o3 with a higher hallucination rate than an earlier OpenAI model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable release evaluations show no higher hallucination rate against the relevant predecessors, or corrected results invalidate the reported increases.
